name: JEE Main
frequency: Twice a year (January and April sessions)
approxCandidates: ≈16 lakh unique registrants across both sessions (2026); ≈13.55 lakh registered for Session 1
eligibility: Class 12 (PCM) passed or appearing in 2026/2027; no age limit (institute-level 75% criterion for NIT/IIIT/CFTI admission)

notification.summary: NTA's tentative exam calendar (notice of 16 Sep 2026, as reported) schedules JEE Main 2027 Session 1 on 22–24 and 28–30 January 2027 with 31 January as a buffer day. The detailed information bulletin and registration had not been released as of 10 Oct 2026; Session 2 dates (April 2027) will come in a separate notice.

pattern.notes: Each subject: Section A = 20 single-correct MCQs (+4/−1), Section B = 5 numerical-value questions (+4/−1, all compulsory since 2025). This mock bank covers the MCQ part only. Scores are normalised across shifts into NTA percentiles; best of the two sessions counts.

trendAnalysis.summary: Since the 2024 syllabus cut (removal of topics such as mathematical reasoning, sets-in-depth, surface chemistry, polymers, solid state, communication systems) the paper has been strictly NCERT-centric. Mathematics is consistently the longest and toughest section, with heavy calculation in calculus, vectors/3D, matrices and probability. Chemistry has tilted toward physical and organic numericals while inorganic stays NCERT-line based (coordination, p-block, d-block). Physics is formula/application driven, with modern physics, electrostatics, current electricity, magnetism and optics giving about half the marks. Removal of choice in Section B from 2025 increased the weight of accurate numericals; overall difficulty is moderate with occasional tough shifts.

pyqBlueprint.method: Compiled from the NTA's officially released JEE Main Paper 1 question papers and answer keys (Jan and Apr sessions 2024–2026) as summarised in public shift-wise analyses (Vedantu, Competishun, Careers360 chapter counts across all 2026 shifts). Web search confirmed chapter-level emphasis (3D/vectors, conics, coordination compounds, ray optics, electrostatics); the question-type patterns were then written from the drafter's own knowledge of the papers, because full paper PDFs could not be fetched. Archetypes describe recurring concept + format + trap in our own words.

archetypes.pattern: Dimensional formula of a constant or derived quantity (h, G, ε₀, μ₀, L/R, RC) or which pair shares dimensions; distractors change one exponent of M, L, T or A
Maximum percentage error in Q = aᵐbⁿ/cᵖ from given % errors; trap: subtracting the error of the denominator or ignoring powers
Body thrown up/down from a tower or balloon: time to reach ground, height or velocity with g = 10 m/s²; trap is the sign of the initial velocity
Projectile on level ground: ratios of heights, ranges or times for two launch angles (often complementary); relation R = 4H cot θ
Static vs kinetic friction: applied force below limiting value so friction equals the applied force; block on rough incline/floor
Connected bodies over a pulley or in contact: acceleration and tension/contact force; distractors from using one mass instead of the total
Kinetic energy–momentum relation p = √(2mK); percentage change of K when p changes or vice versa
Work by a position-dependent force F(x) via integration, or power delivered; distractor from evaluating F at one point
Rod/disc/ring released or rolling: energy conservation including rotational KE gives ω or end/centre speed
Moment of inertia using parallel/perpendicular-axis theorem for rod, ring, disc or combinations about non-central axes
Conservation of angular momentum (person on turntable, disc placed on disc): final ω or ratio of kinetic energies
Orbital/escape energy: energy to shift a satellite between orbits or to escape, expressed in m, g, R
Variation of g with height and depth (compare points), satellite period ratios via Kepler’s third law
Surface tension: excess pressure in drops/bubbles, coalescence of bubbles or drops, work done to form/split drops
Young’s modulus: ratio of extensions for wires of different length/radius under same load; elastic energy; thermal stress
Fluid flow: continuity + Bernoulli pressure difference, efflux speed, terminal velocity (Stokes’ law)
First law in isobaric/isochoric/isothermal processes: fraction of heat used as work or ΔU, using Cp and Cv
Carnot engine/refrigerator: efficiency, heat rejected, COP; adiabatic T–V/P–V relations
rms/mean/most-probable speed scaling with T and M; degrees of freedom, Cv and γ of gas mixtures
Stretched string or organ pipe: harmonic frequencies when tension, length or end conditions change
SHM: energy at a displacement, time period of spring/pendulum combinations, phase relations
Charge sharing between capacitors and energy loss; series/parallel combinations with dielectrics
Field/potential of continuous distributions (ring, arc, rod, semicircle, sphere) at special points
Gauss’s law flux through a cube or part of a closed surface; work in moving charges; electrostatic potential energy
Equivalent resistance and branch current in series–parallel networks with ideal/real cells
Wheatstone/metre bridge/potentiometer balance; resistance change when a wire is stretched; drift velocity
Magnetic moment/field of rotating charged ring or disc, field at centre of loops and arcs
Charged particle in uniform B: radius/period comparison for proton, deuteron, α-particle with same KE, V or momentum
Force between parallel currents, torque on a coil, conversion of galvanometer to ammeter/voltmeter (shunt/series resistance)
Series LCR: resonant frequency, impedance, power factor and average power
Motional emf of a rod on rails/rotating rod, induced current and retarding force; flux change in coils
Plane EM wave: E₀ = cB₀, intensity/energy density, ordering of spectrum and uses
Lens maker’s formula: focal length/power change when lens is immersed in a liquid or combined with another lens
YDSE: fringe width changes with medium/wavelength/slit spacing, positions of bright and dark fringes
Prism minimum deviation, critical angle/TIR, apparent depth; mirror-formula image position
de Broglie wavelength of accelerated particles; photoelectric equation, stopping potential and threshold
Bohr model: wavelength ratios of series lines (Lyman/Balmer/Paschen), energy/radius of nth orbit for H-like ions
Radioactivity: half-life/mean-life, fraction decayed; number of α and β decays in a chain; mass defect and binding energy
Combination of logic gates — truth table/output; diode and Zener circuits
Stoichiometry from a balanced equation: mass/volume at STP of reactant or product, limiting reagent
Concentration conversions: % w/w or density to molality/molarity/mole fraction
Radial/angular nodes, allowed quantum-number sets, number of orbitals/electrons for given n, l, m
Bohr energy/radius/velocity for H-like species; de Broglie and uncertainty relations
Dipole moment (zero vs non-zero) from VSEPR geometry; count of polar molecules in a list
MOT: bond order and magnetic behaviour of O₂, N₂, C₂ and their ions; ordering of bond order/length
Hybridisation, shape and lone pairs of xenon fluorides, interhalogens and polyatomic ions
Spontaneity from ΔG = ΔH − TΔS (crossover temperature); ΔH − ΔU = ΔnRT
Hess’s law: enthalpy of formation/combustion from given enthalpies; bond-enthalpy calculations
Colligative property with van’t Hoff factor for electrolytes/complexes (ΔTf, ΔTb, π)
Raoult’s law: total vapour pressure and vapour-phase mole fraction for ideal binary mixtures
pH of strong acid/base mixtures, buffers (Henderson equation) and salt hydrolysis
Ksp and solubility, common-ion effect; Kp–Kc and degree of dissociation
Nernst equation emf of a cell with given concentrations; ΔG° = −nFE°
Faraday’s laws (charge/mass deposited, n-factor from change in oxidation state); Kohlrausch law
First-order integrated law: time for x% completion vs half-life, fraction left after n half-lives
Order from initial-rate data / rate law; Arrhenius equation with k at two temperatures
Ordering of ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, radii with the standard exceptions (N > O, Mg > Al, Cl > F)
Structure of oxoacids/oxides (P₄O₁₀, H₃PO₃, H₂S₂O₈, oxoacids of S/Cl): count of bonds, bridges, P–OH groups
Group trends: thermal stability/acidity of hydrides, inert-pair effect, oxidising power; correct order or statement
Spin-only magnetic moment/colour of 3d ions; oxidation states
Stoichiometry/oxidation of KMnO₄ and K₂Cr₂O₇ in acid; lanthanoid contraction consequences
VBT/CFT: hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature of a complex (strong vs weak field ligands)
Counting geometrical/optical isomers of octahedral and square-planar complexes
CFSE in units of Δo, spin-only moment of complexes, IUPAC names
Stability order of carbocations/radicals/carbanions via resonance, hyperconjugation and inductive effects
Acidity/basicity order of substituted phenols, acids and amines (−I, −M, ortho effects)
Qualitative/quantitative analysis of organic compounds (Lassaigne, Kjeldahl, Carius) and purification methods
Ozonolysis products; Markovnikov vs peroxide (anti-Markovnikov) additions to alkenes
Aromaticity (Hückel rule), directive influence in electrophilic substitution, alkyne reactions
Elimination (Saytzeff) vs substitution products; SN1/SN2 reactivity order of halides
Named reactions of phenol (Kolbe, Reimer–Tiemann), acidity of phenols, Lucas test, ether cleavage with HI
Distinguishing tests (iodoform, Tollens’, Fehling’s) — which compound gives which result
Named reactions: aldol, Cannizzaro, HVZ, Clemmensen/Wolff–Kishner — identify the product
Hinsberg test, basicity order of amines in water, diazonium salt conversions
Reducing/non-reducing sugars, glycosidic linkages, vitamins and nucleic-acid bases
Salt analysis: flame colours, coloured precipitates for cations/anions, indicator choice in titration
Domain/range of composite log/root/inverse-trig functions
Relations: checking reflexive/symmetric/transitive, counting relations or functions on small sets
Powers of i, (1 ± i)/(1 ∓ i) and cube roots of unity
Locus and modulus–argument: max/min of |z| under |z − z₀| = r type conditions
Symmetric functions of roots (α³ + β³, α⁴ + β⁴, α/β + β/α) and transformed equations
Number of real roots of equations with |x| or reducible to quadratics
Properties |kA|, |adj A|, |adj(adj A)|, |A⁻¹| for n × n matrices
System of linear equations: λ, μ for unique / infinitely many / no solutions
Matrix algebra: A² − kA + mI = O, powers of a matrix, symmetric/skew-symmetric parts
Arrangements of letters with repetition and restrictions (together/not together, vowels at even places), word rank
Selections with constraints (committee with at least k of a kind), distribution of objects
Term independent of x or coefficient of xᵏ via the general term
Remainder of large powers using binomial expansion; sums of binomial coefficients
Arithmetico-geometric sums Σk·xᵏ (finite or infinite), telescoping sums
AP/GP terms and sums from two given conditions; AM–GM inequality
Standard trigonometric/exponential limits, 0/0 and 1^∞ forms
Constants making a piecewise function continuous/differentiable; points of non-differentiability
Maxima/minima of geometric quantities; intervals of increase/decrease
Definite integral by King’s property ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = ∫ₐᵇ f(a + b − x) dx
Definite integrals with greatest-integer/modulus functions by splitting the interval
Indefinite integral by substitution or partial fractions; identify the antiderivative
Area between two curves (parabola–parabola, parabola–line) using intersection points
Linear first-order DE with integrating factor and initial condition; value at a point
Homogeneous or variable-separable DE; family/order–degree questions
Distance between parallel lines, foot of perpendicular, angle bisectors, area of triangle
Length of tangent, chord length, common chord, orthogonal circles
Tangent to parabola/ellipse with given slope (c = a/m, c² = a²m² + b²)
Eccentricity, latus rectum, foci of ellipse/hyperbola from given conditions
Shortest distance between skew lines in vector or Cartesian form
Foot/image of a point in a plane or line, angle between line and plane, distance of point from plane
Magnitudes |a ± b|, dot/cross products and angle between vectors
Scalar triple product: coplanarity condition, volume of parallelepiped; vector triple product
Mean/variance after correcting, adding or transforming observations
Bayes’ theorem with two urns/bags or a test with error rates
Addition/multiplication rules for independent events; binomial distribution probabilities
Number of solutions of a trigonometric equation in a given interval; max/min of trig expressions

resources.notes: NTA posts each shift's question paper with provisional and final answer keys on jeemain.nta.nic.in after the exam (candidates can view their response sheets). Practice/mock tests are hosted by NTA (nta.ac.in, NTA mock test portal). Archive papers for 2019 onward are widely mirrored by coaching sites, but only the NTA copies are official.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 20 m/s from the top of a tower 25 m high. How long does it take to reach the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Taking upward positive: −25 = 20t − 5t² ⇒ t² − 4t − 5 = 0 ⇒ (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0 ⇒ t = 5 s.

relevance.note: Faithful tower-throw item; sign trap and -1 s root handled; typical 2024 Main numbers

questions.question: A 2 kg block rests on a rough horizontal floor (coefficient of static friction 0.3). A horizontal force of 4 N is applied to it. The frictional force acting on the block is (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Limiting friction = μmg = 0.3 × 2 × 10 = 6 N. Since the applied 4 N is less than 6 N, the block stays at rest and static friction equals the applied force, 4 N.

relevance.note: Classic Main static-friction trap (4 N < 6 N limiting) with 6 N distractor exactly as set

questions.question: A uniform rod of length L is hinged at one end and released from rest in the horizontal position. When it becomes vertical, the speed of its free end is
questions.explanation: Loss of PE = mgL/2 = ½(mL²/3)ω² ⇒ ω = √(3g/L). Speed of free end = ωL = √(3gL).

relevance.note: Hinged rod released from horizontal, end speed √(3gL) is a recurring Main item; good distractors

questions.question: A satellite of mass m moves in a circular orbit of radius 2R around the Earth (radius R, surface gravity g). The minimum energy needed to shift it to a circular orbit of radius 3R is
questions.explanation: Total energy in orbit r is −GMm/2r. ΔE = GMm/2(1/2R − 1/3R) = GMm/(12R). With GM = gR², ΔE = mgR/12.

relevance.note: Orbit-transfer energy GMm/12R in mgR form matches Main gravitation PYQs closely

questions.question: Two soap bubbles of radii 3 cm and 4 cm coalesce in vacuum under isothermal conditions to form a single bubble. The radius of the new bubble is
questions.explanation: In vacuum the inside pressure is 4T/r. Isothermal: Σ pV is conserved ⇒ (4T/r)(4πr³/3) ∝ r², so R² = 3² + 4² = 25 ⇒ R = 5 cm.

relevance.note: Bubble coalescence in vacuum r²=r1²+r2² is a known Main question; 3-4-5 numbers faithful

questions.question: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas is heated at constant pressure. The fraction of the heat supplied that is used to do external work is
questions.explanation: W = nRΔT and Q = nCpΔT = n(5R/2)ΔT. W/Q = R/(5R/2) = 2/5.

relevance.note: Isobaric W/Q = R/Cp = 2/5 is a repeated Main 1-mark style item; distractors 3/5, 2/3 apt

questions.question: The rms speed of the molecules of a gas at 27 °C is v. At what temperature will the rms speed become 2v?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T. Doubling speed needs 4T = 4 × 300 K = 1200 K = 927 °C.

relevance.note: rms speed ×2 → T×4 with °C trap (1200 vs 927) mirrors Main KTG items

questions.question: A 4 μF capacitor charged to 50 V is connected across an identical uncharged 4 μF capacitor. The energy lost in the process is
questions.explanation: Initial energy = ½ × 4×10⁻⁶ × 50² = 5 mJ. Common potential = 25 V; final energy = ½ × 8×10⁻⁶ × 25² = 2.5 mJ. Loss = 2.5 mJ.

relevance.note: Charge sharing between identical capacitors, energy loss half, standard Main archetype

questions.question: A thin semicircular ring of radius R carries a total charge Q uniformly distributed. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is
questions.explanation: For a semicircular arc with λ = Q/(πR), the horizontal components cancel and E = 2kλ/R = 2Q/(4πε₀·πR²) = Q/(2π²ε₀R²).

relevance.note: Semicircular ring field Q/(2π²ε0R²) is a well-known Main PYQ form with factor-of-2 distractors

questions.question: A thin non-conducting disc of radius R carries charge Q spread uniformly over its surface and rotates about its axis with angular velocity ω. Its magnetic dipole moment is
questions.explanation: A ring of radius r, width dr has charge dq = (Q/πR²)2πr dr and moment dM = (dq·ω/2π)πr² = (Qω/R²)r³ dr. Integrating 0 to R gives QωR²/4.

relevance.note: Rotating charged disc moment QωR²/4 is an established Main PYQ; distractors by factor errors

questions.question: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform magnetic field perpendicular to it with equal kinetic energies. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths (r_p : r_α) is
questions.explanation: r = √(2mK)/(qB). For α: √(2·4m·K)/(2eB) = 2√(2mK)/(2eB) = √(2mK)/(eB), the same as for the proton. So the ratio is 1 : 1.

relevance.note: Proton vs α same KE radius 1:1 is a frequently repeated Main question

questions.question: A thin convex lens of focal length 20 cm in air is made of glass of refractive index 1.5. When immersed in water (refractive index 4/3), its focal length becomes

relevance.note: Lens immersed in water focal length ×4 → 80 cm, classic Main lens-maker question

questions.question: The ratio of the longest wavelength of the Lyman series to the longest wavelength of the Balmer series in the hydrogen spectrum is

relevance.note: Lyman/Balmer longest-wavelength ratio 5:27 with reciprocal distractor is a repeated Main item

questions.question: The numbers of radial and angular nodes in a 4d orbital are respectively
questions.explanation: Angular nodes = l = 2; radial nodes = n − l − 1 = 4 − 2 − 1 = 1.

relevance.note: Radial/angular nodes of 4d; Main asks this, one-step formula

questions.question: The correct order of bond order of the following species is
questions.explanation: From MO theory: O₂⁺ = 2.5, O₂ = 2, O₂⁻ = 1.5, O₂²⁻ = 1.

relevance.note: O2 species bond-order ordering, exactly the Main MOT archetype

questions.question: For a reaction ΔH = −40 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = −100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ (both assumed temperature-independent). Above what temperature does the reaction become non-spontaneous?
questions.explanation: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = 0 at T = ΔH/ΔS = (−40000)/(−100) = 400 K. Above 400 K, −TΔS dominates and ΔG > 0.

relevance.note: Crossover T = ΔH/ΔS with unit trap (J vs kJ, 40 K / 4000 K distractors) – faithful

questions.question: The depression in freezing point of a 0.1 molal aqueous solution of K₄[Fe(CN)₆], assuming complete dissociation, is (K_f of water = 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: K₄[Fe(CN)₆] → 4K⁺ + [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻, so i = 5. ΔT_f = iK_f m = 5 × 1.86 × 0.1 = 0.93 K.

relevance.note: K4[Fe(CN)6] i=5 ΔTf, typical Main van't Hoff question

questions.question: 50 mL of 0.2 M HCl is mixed with 50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH. The pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation: H⁺ = 10 mmol, OH⁻ = 5 mmol; excess H⁺ = 5 mmol in 100 mL = 0.05 M. pH = −log 0.05 = 1.30.

relevance.note: Strong acid–base mixture pH with dilution trap; standard Main

questions.question: For the cell Zn | Zn²⁺(0.01 M) || Cu²⁺(1 M) | Cu at 298 K, E°cell = 1.10 V. The emf of the cell is (take 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V)

relevance.note: Nernst for Daniell cell with sign trap (1.041 distractor) faithful to Main

questions.question: For a first-order reaction, the time required for 99.9% completion is approximately how many times its half-life?

relevance.note: t99.9 ≈ 10 t½; repeatedly asked; 3.32/6.64 distractors from log mistakes

questions.question: The correct order of first ionisation enthalpy is
questions.explanation: B < Be because B's 2p electron is easier to remove than Be's 2s; O < N because N has a stable half-filled 2p³ configuration.

relevance.note: IE order with Be>B and N>O exceptions – exact Main periodicity pattern

questions.question: The number of P–O–P bridging bonds in a molecule of P₄O₁₀ is
questions.explanation: In P₄O₁₀ each P is bonded to one terminal O and three bridging O atoms; there are 6 bridging oxygens, i.e. six P–O–P linkages.

relevance.note: P4O10 bridging O count 6, a frequent Main structure question

questions.question: The hybridisation, geometry and magnetic nature of [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ are
questions.explanation: Ni²⁺ is 3d⁸. Strong-field CN⁻ pairs the electrons, leaving one 3d orbital empty for dsp² hybridisation: square planar with no unpaired electrons.

relevance.note: [Ni(CN)4]2- dsp2 square planar diamagnetic; textbook VBT example, frequently asked

questions.question: The total number of stereoisomers possible for [Co(en)₂Cl₂]⁺ is
questions.explanation: It has cis and trans forms; the cis form is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers, while trans is achiral. Total = 2 + 1 = 3.

relevance.note: [Co(en)2Cl2]+ stereoisomers 3, staple Main isomer count

questions.question: Which of the following carbocations is the most stable?
questions.explanation: The triphenylmethyl cation is delocalised over three benzene rings, giving far greater resonance stabilisation than the benzyl, allyl or tert-butyl cations.

relevance.note: Trityl cation most stable; GOC staple, slightly easy

questions.question: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene followed by reductive work-up (Zn/H₂O) gives
questions.explanation: (CH₃)₂C=CH–CH₃ cleaves at the double bond to give (CH₃)₂C=O (propanone) and CH₃CHO (ethanal).

relevance.note: Ozonolysis of 2-methylbut-2-ene to acetone+ethanal, standard Main product ID

questions.question: Which compound gives a positive iodoform test but does NOT reduce Tollens' reagent?
questions.explanation: Pentan-2-one has a CH₃CO– group (iodoform positive) and, being a ketone, does not reduce Tollens'. Ethanal gives both tests; propanal gives only Tollens'; pentan-3-one gives neither.

relevance.note: Iodoform-positive but Tollens-negative ketone; good discriminating distractors (ethanal)

questions.question: Which amine forms a product with benzenesulphonyl chloride that is soluble in aqueous alkali?
questions.explanation: A primary amine forms N-ethylbenzenesulphonamide, which has an acidic N–H and dissolves in alkali. Secondary amines give alkali-insoluble products; tertiary amines do not react.

relevance.note: Hinsberg: 1° amine sulphonamide alkali-soluble; faithful

questions.question: The domain of f(x) = √(log₁₀((5x − x²)/4)) is
questions.explanation: We need (5x − x²)/4 ≥ 1 ⇒ x² − 5x + 4 ≤ 0 ⇒ (x − 1)(x − 4) ≤ 0 ⇒ 1 ≤ x ≤ 4 (the argument is then positive automatically).

relevance.note: Domain of √log quadratic giving [1,4] with open/closed interval traps – Main style

questions.question: If z = (1 + i)/(1 − i), then z²⁰²⁶ equals

relevance.note: ((1+i)/(1−i))^2026 = −1 uses current-year exponent, typical Main

questions.question: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 4, then |adj(2A)| equals
questions.explanation: |2A| = 2³ × 4 = 32. For a 3×3 matrix, |adj B| = |B|², so |adj(2A)| = 32² = 1024.

relevance.note: |adj(2A)| = (2³·4)² = 1024 with scalar-power trap – faithful Main

questions.question: The system x + y + z = 6, x + 2y + 3z = 10, x + 2y + λz = μ has infinitely many solutions when
questions.explanation: Subtracting the second equation from the third: (λ − 3)z = μ − 10. Infinitely many solutions need 0·z = 0, i.e. λ = 3 and μ = 10 (the first two equations are independent).

relevance.note: λ, μ for infinitely many solutions – exact Main archetype with ≠ distractors

questions.question: The number of arrangements of the letters of the word BANANA in which the two N's are not together is
questions.explanation: Total = 6!/(3!2!) = 60. With NN as one block: 5!/3! = 20. Required = 60 − 20 = 40.

relevance.note: BANANA with N's not together 40 via complement – Main P&C style

questions.question: The term independent of x in the expansion of (x² + 1/x)⁹ is

relevance.note: Term independent of x in (x²+1/x)^9 = 84; standard general-term item

questions.question: The value of Σ (k = 1 to 10) k·2ᵏ is

relevance.note: Σk·2^k AGP closed form 18434 with near-miss distractors – Main-like

questions.question: The value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of sin x/(sin x + cos x) dx is
questions.explanation: Let I be the integral. Replacing x by π/2 − x gives the same integral with cos x on top; adding, 2I = ∫ 1 dx = π/2, so I = π/4.

relevance.note: King's property sin/(sin+cos) = π/4; very well-known, easy for Main

questions.question: The value of ∫ from 0 to 2 of [x²] dx, where [·] denotes the greatest integer function, is

relevance.note: ∫[x²] over 0..2 = 5−√2−√3, exact Main PYQ type with sign-swap distractors

questions.question: The area bounded by the parabolas y² = 4x and x² = 4y is
questions.explanation: They meet at (0,0) and (4,4). Area = ∫ from 0 to 4 of (2√x − x²/4) dx = 32/3 − 16/3 = 16/3.

relevance.note: Area between y²=4x and x²=4y = 16/3 – classic Main

questions.question: If dy/dx + y/x = x² and y(1) = 1, then y(2) equals
questions.explanation: Integrating factor x: d(xy)/dx = x³ ⇒ xy = x⁴/4 + C. y(1) = 1 ⇒ C = 3/4. At x = 2: 2y = 4 + 3/4 ⇒ y = 19/8.

relevance.note: Linear DE with IF x and IC, y(2)=19/8 – Main style

questions.question: The distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y − 7 = 0 and 6x + 8y + 6 = 0 is
questions.explanation: Second line is 3x + 4y + 3 = 0. Distance = |−7 − 3|/√(9 + 16) = 10/5 = 2.

relevance.note: Parallel lines distance with coefficient-normalisation trap – exactly Main's trap

questions.question: The shortest distance between the lines r = (î + ĵ) + λ(2î − ĵ + k̂) and r = (2î + ĵ − k̂) + μ(3î − 5ĵ + 2k̂) is

relevance.note: Skew-line shortest distance 10/√59 verified; Main 3D staple

questions.question: If |a| = 3, |b| = 4 and |a + b| = 5, then |a − b| equals

relevance.note: Parallelogram law |a−b| = 5; Main-type but light

questions.question: The mean and variance of five observations are 6 and 4. If one observation equal to 10 is replaced by 7, the new variance is

relevance.note: Variance after replacing an observation (0.64) – frequent Main statistics PYQ

questions.question: The dimensional formula of the permittivity of free space ε₀ is
questions.explanation: From Coulomb’s law ε₀ = q²/(4πFr²) = (AT)²/([MLT⁻²][L²]) = [M⁻¹ L⁻³ T⁴ A²]. [M L T⁻² A⁻²] is the dimension of μ₀.

relevance.note: ε0 dimensions with exponent-swap distractors – archetype exact

questions.question: A physical quantity is given by Q = a³b²/(c√d). The percentage errors in a, b, c and d are 1%, 2%, 3% and 4% respectively. The maximum percentage error in Q is
questions.explanation: Maximum error = 3(1) + 2(2) + 1(3) + ½(4) = 3 + 4 + 3 + 2 = 12%. Errors always add, even for quantities in the denominator.

relevance.note: Max % error with √d half-power trap – Main style

questions.question: Blocks of mass 3 kg and 2 kg hang at the two ends of a light inextensible string passing over a smooth, massless pulley. The tension in the string is (g = 10 m/s²)

questions.question: The moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass M and radius R about a tangent lying in the plane of the disc is
questions.explanation: About a diameter I = MR²/4 (perpendicular-axis theorem). A tangent in the plane is parallel to a diameter at distance R: I = MR²/4 + MR² = 5MR²/4. (3MR²/2 is for a tangent perpendicular to the plane.)

relevance.note: Disc about in-plane tangent 5MR²/4, the classic Main parallel/perp-axis item

questions.question: A person stands on a platform rotating freely about a vertical axis; the moment of inertia of the system is 6 kg m². When the person stretches out the arms, the moment of inertia becomes 8 kg m². The ratio of the final to the initial rotational kinetic energy is
questions.explanation: Angular momentum L is conserved and K = L²/(2I), so K_f/K_i = I_i/I_f = 6/8 = 3/4.

questions.question: At what height above the Earth’s surface is the acceleration due to gravity the same as at a depth of R/2 below the surface? (R = radius of the Earth)
questions.explanation: At depth R/2: g′ = g(1 − 1/2) = g/2. At height h: gR²/(R + h)² = g/2 ⇒ R + h = √2R ⇒ h = (√2 − 1)R.

relevance.note: g at height equals g at depth R/2 → (√2−1)R; Main PYQ type

questions.question: Two wires A and B are made of the same material. A has length L and diameter d; B has length 2L and diameter 2d. They are stretched by the same load. The ratio of their extensions ΔL_A : ΔL_B is
questions.explanation: ΔL = FL/(AY) ∝ L/d². A: L/d²; B: 2L/(4d²) = L/(2d²). Ratio = 2 : 1.

questions.question: Water flows steadily through a horizontal pipe. At a section of area A the speed is 2 m/s; at another section of area A/2 the pressure is lower. The pressure difference between the two sections is (density of water = 1000 kg/m³)
questions.explanation: Continuity: v₂ = 2 × 2 = 4 m/s. Bernoulli: ΔP = ½ρ(v₂² − v₁²) = ½ × 1000 × (16 − 4) = 6000 Pa = 6 kPa.

questions.explanation: A NAND output is 0 only when both its inputs are 1, i.e. A = 1 and A + B = 1. With A = 1, A + B = 1 for any B, so (1, 0) and (1, 1).

questions.question: If α and β are the roots of x² − 3x + 1 = 0, then α⁴ + β⁴ equals

questions.question: If A is a 3 × 3 matrix with |A| = 3, then |adj(adj A)| equals
